opportunities.title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space! A learning circle is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment. Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field. In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to: transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel query data from a relational database using SQL improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau We will meet weekly, in-person, every Tuesday afternoon, September 15 - December 8, 2-3:30 PM (12 sessions). Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis. Learners who complete the course will be able to: earn a digital badge download a certificate of completion

opportunities.title: Word Basics 2: Format a Flyer
opportunities.description: Build on your basic Microsoft Word skills and learn to use Word more effectively. In this class, you will: Practice new Word skills while you design a flyer Format text, margins, indents, headers and footers Format text as columns Create bulleted, numbered and sorted lists Review your document with Spelling and Grammar check and Thesaurus Upon completion of this class, you will be able to use even more Word tools to design your documents. Prerequisites: Word Basics 1 or equivalent skills. Basic keyboarding and mouse skills required. Format: Hands-on with demonstrations

opportunities.title: Youth Hub: Disassemble a Desktop Computer
opportunities.description: Have you ever wondered what's going on inside a computer? Ever wanted to take apart a computer to see? This workshop is your chance! During this workshop, we'll go over what's inside a computer, how to properly open a desktop, and safety guidelines to follow when it comes to working with electronics. This program is part of Youth Hub service. Youth Hubs are a welcoming place for teens after school and in the summer, where helpful staff are always available. Free, nutritious snacks are offered daily. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.description: Looking for something to do after school? Come out to our After School Club and learn new things, make stuff, meet other kids and have fun! For ages 6-12. Snacks are offered during the After School Club for participants. Ingredient lists will be available. Snacks are generously supported, in part, by donors. September: Marble Run Marble Run is a fun track where marbles roll down using gravity. Children can build tracks with tubes, ramps, and tunnels, then watch the marbles race to the finish. In this program, kids will explore, create, test, and improve their own marble runs. They will learn about gravity, speed, and problem-solving while having fun. Let's build, play, and discover together!

opportunities.title: Youth Hub: Fuze Beads
opportunities.description: Join us on Tuesday to create some Fuze Bead designs with the Cricut/iron on machine in the Youth Hub! All teens are welcome! Drop-in, no registration required. Tuesday, September 29, 4-5pm If you identify as a person with a disability or as a person who is Deaf, and require an accessibility accommodation to participate in this program, please contact Accessibility Services by email accessibleservices@tpl.ca, or voicemail, 416-393-7099, to make a request. Please contact us at least three weeks in advance. This program is part of Youth Hub service. Youth Hubs are a welcoming place for teens after school and in the summer, where helpful staff are always available. Free, nutritious snacks are offered daily. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Vector Design with Adobe Illustrator
opportunities.description: This is a 2-part series, participants are expected to attend both sessions. Learn how to make digital art in Adobe Illustrator. We will talk about the differences between vector and raster images, explore some of the tools at our disposal, and then use these tools to design a small vector drawing. In the second class we will learn more advanced techniques. This class is for beginners but assumes you have a basic understanding of computer skills. opportunities.title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles! What You'll Learn This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover: Essential Prompting Skills : How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results. Everyday Work Tasks: Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more. Data & Presentations: How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data. Advanced Techniques: How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time. Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions. Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once for the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address. A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, Sept 8, 15, 22 and 29. Registration is a two-step process. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Coding with Python III
opportunities.description: Python is an open source programming language that is used for creating web applications, web content, mathematics and system scripting. In this follow up course we will really start to stretch our legs in Python, designing and implementing some simple Object Oriented Programming data structures. Key takeaways will include a working knowledge of Python classes and objects. This class is for beginners but assumes you have a basic understanding of Python or have attended Coding with Python I and II. Registration will start 2 weeks before this class . This program is hosted on Zoom. The Zoom information and link will be shared over email. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca, 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

Note: Customers are no longer required to attend a mandatory 3D printing class prior to using a 3D printer at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class is for those who are interested in learning more about 3D printing and how to use the Prusa software.

opportunities.title: After School Club
opportunities.description: Looking for something to do after school? Come out to our After School Club and learn new things, make stuff, play games, try out our robotics, meet other kids and have fun! For ages 6-12. Drop-in. Snacks are offered during the After School Club for participants. If you or your child lives with a disability, and requires an accessibility accommodation to participate in this program, please contact Accessibility Services by email, accessibleservices@tpl.ca, or voicemail, 416-393-7099, to make a request. Please contact us at least three weeks in advance.
opportunities.address: Taylor Memorial, 1440 Kingston Road, Toronto, ON, M1N 1R3

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Markham Village
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity
opportunities.description: Want to learn how to add custom audio to your films and videos? Perhaps a voiceover? Join us in our Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity workshop! Audacity is an easy-to-use, multi-track audio editor and recorder for Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux and other operating systems. Audacity is a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) that is FREE to download. This makerspace demonstration will provide instruction on how to use this program to get you started with sound editing and recording. We will cover how to edit sound, what effects this program has to offer on your vocals and how to mix down your different tracks. At the end of the session you will receive a quick tour of Markham Village's sound booth and more information on how to book the space. With your new skills, why not participate in our upcoming Markham Village Film Festival ? Hope to see you there. Become Maker Certified Please note: if you are looking to use our makerspaces independently, you must be 13+ and complete this online Makerspace module . Once completed, our staff can update your profile and you will be maker certified!
opportunities.address: Markham Village Branch, 6031 Highway 7, Markham, Ontario, L3P 3A7

opportunities.title: Data Analytics Essentials Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space! A learning circle is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment. Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field. In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to: transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel query data from a relational database using SQL improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau We will meet online every Thursday evening, September 24 - December 10, 6-7:30 PM (12 sessions). Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis. Learners who complete the course will be able to: earn a digital badge download a certificate of completion

opportunities.title: Google AI Essentials: In Person Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization. This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz. By completing the specialization, you will learn: How AI works How to write effective prompts How to use generative AI tools responsibly How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm How to stay up to date with AI news After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions. No AI experience is required. How to Join a Learning Circle: Register once on the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address . A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions in person at Northern District Branch . Registration is a two-step procedure. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: AI Everywhere, All At Once
opportunities.description: AI is suddenly everywhere, in ads, on your phone, your news feed, all your software, even your search bar. Who decides what gets made with AI? What does it cost? And what does it feel like? What happens when these tools start to feel less like tools and more like collaborators? In this kickoff event for our Innovator in Residence (Applied AI Development) program, join Ryan Kelln for an illustrated talk with live demos. Let's think together deeply about the impact, costs and opportunities presented when trillions of dollars are spent researching and developing digital intelligence. We'll talk candidly about the people who make it, why they make it, and how it shifts power. Then we'll look at what your library can offer that the AI companies can't, and how to get the most out of the 12 week residency program ahead. Registration is required and will start September 9, 2026 at 9:00 AM. Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program. After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.description: AI technologies have become increasingly prevalent in many aspects of modern life, including healthcare, finance, transportation, and entertainment. Come join this beginner in-person class to learn what AI is, how it learns and predicts outcomes, considerations when using GenAI applications, and how the Internet of Things (IOT) applies to AI. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. opportunities.description: Learn how 3D printers work and how you can print at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class includes hands-on instruction with Prusa Slicer, the software used to prepare your 3D object file for printing on a Prusa MK3S+ 3D printer. DROP IN Note: Customers are no longer required to attend a mandatory 3D printing class prior to using a 3D printer at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class is for those who are interested in learning more about 3D printing and how to use the Prusa software.

opportunities.title: Jill Lepore: The Artificial State
opportunities.description: TPL and Toronto Metropolitan University present Pulitzer-Prize winning historian Jill Lepore in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon. As Professor of American History at Harvard University and Professor of Law at Harvard Law School, Jill Lepore brings her rare gift for narrative history to one of the most urgent questions of our time: has democracy already been quietly replaced by rule of a different kind, one governed not by citizens, but by machines owned by corporations? In her new book The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State , Lepore traces our increasing dependence on and strangulation by data. Framing the book as a successor to Hannah Arendt's The Origins of Totalitarianism , Lepore shares a new history for our twenty-first century. What does it mean when the era of the liberal nation-state seems to be giving way to the rule of artificial intelligence? Lepore insists history is driven not by machines but by individuals, societies, cultures, and ideas, and that the architects of the Artificial State drew their governing philosophy not from science, but from science fiction. Can what has been built be undone? And what would it take to reimagine a genuinely democratic relationship between technology and self-governance, one where humans, not machines, remain accountable to one another? Join one of America's most celebrated historians, fresh from her bestselling We the People: A History of the U.S. Constitution , for an essential conversation about power, technology, and the fight to reclaim democratic life from the architects of an artificial future. Question and answer session and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase. About this Event's Guests: Jill Lepore Sanjay Ruparelia Read More: Rise and Fall of the Artificial State We the People *** This event is part of our On Civil Society series, where we host local and international authors, activists and academics in conversation about the most critical topics of our time. Generously supported by the McConnell Foundation and also by Chris M. Reid. *** About the series: On the Frontlines of Democracy is a public lecture series to analyze the trajectory of democracy in the twenty-first century. In every region, the prospects of democracy face serious challenges, old and new. Can we protect constitutional rights and renew collective self-rule in an era of popular mistrust, severe partisanship and resurgent nationalism? Can they reduce inequalities of power, wealth and status, defend deep diversity and confront climate change in the new digital age? Can we develop innovative strategies to revitalize civic engagement, empower public institutions and resist autocratic threats? And what can we offer, learn and do to promote the prospects of democracy in our increasingly post-western global order? *** PLAN YOUR VISIT : Location: Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor Time: Doors open 6:00 pm, Event starts 7 pm. Tickets: Free registration required. Ticket policy: Tickets guaranteed until 6:50 pm, after which rush line admission begins. Seating first come, first served. Bar: Beer/wine available for purchase (debit/credit only). TPL is committed to accessibility. If you are Deaf or have a disability and would like to request accommodation for this event, please contact accessibleservices@tpl.ca or 416-393-7099 at least three weeks prior to the event. *** Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Registrants may be contacted to fill out a brief survey following the program . Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca, 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Thornhill Community Centre
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM. These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Let's Tell Silly Stories Around The ‘Campfire’ + STEAM Challenge with friends and family! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.description: Join our G1-G2 level Tips and Fun with Math virtually, where students can sit comfortably at home while receiving classroom quality math deliverables, develop basic logic and arithmetic skills, a general understanding of geometry, and practice simple word problems! We see the importance of building a solid foundation for student’s early math knowledge, and aim to guide their development with useful tricks and joy! - U+ Tips and Fun with Math - a creative and logical solution. - Materials will be provided. Parents participation is not required. Please note these sessions are on a monthly basis (please sign up for each class to receive the link): - Oct 5 - Nov 2 - Dec 7

opportunities.title: Be An Active Digital Citizen - Play-based Workshop for Families
opportunities.description: In this play-based, interactive workshop for children and families, we explore what it means to be a smart, safe, and empowered digital citizen. Through games and hands-on activities, children will practice healthy social media habits and learn about their digital rights online in a fun, age-appropriate way. At the end of this workshop, participants should: Be able to recognize healthy vs. unhealthy social media habits and practice simple strategies for balanced use. Understand basic digital rights for children online (i.e. privacy, safety, expression). Build confidence identifying safe, respectful ways to engage with others online, both individually and as a family. Note: this session is intended to be intended by families including children aged 8 - 16 and their parents/caregivers . Please register for each individual attending. Hosted by Kids Rights Canada .

opportunities.title: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams
opportunities.description: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams which addresses the growing threat of AI-enabled online fraud and scams targeting older Canadians. As AI tools become more accessible, scammers are using tactics such as voice cloning, deepfake videos, and highly convincing phishing techniques to impersonate loved ones and fabricate financial emergencies. Older adults aged 55+ are disproportionately targeted, often experiencing significant financial loss along with shame, anxiety, and social isolation. Through workshops delivered by MediaSmarts experts participants will learn how AI-enabled scams work, how to verify messages from family or financial institutions, and what steps to take if targeted.

opportunities.title: How We Stay Relevant in the Age of AI
opportunities.description: AI is changing how people think about work, learning, and human value. Many professionals, parents, students, and community members are asking a very real question: if AI can generate answers, summaries, explanations, drafts, code, and ideas so quickly, where do humans remain relevant? This session argues that humans should not try to compete with AI at speed, recall, or routine output. That is the wrong competition. As AI makes answers easier to produce, human value moves toward deeper understanding, disciplined curiosity, judgment, and the ability to question, verify, and ground what AI produces. For most of us, learning has often been treated as natural and implicit. We were taught subjects in school, but not always taught how learning itself works. Machine learning gives us a useful mirror. In order to teach machines how to learn, humans had to make parts of learning explicit: objectives, data, patterns, prediction, feedback, error correction, validation, calibration, and updating. This session uses those machine learning principles not as a technical lesson, but as a way to think about how humans can learn more deeply in the age of AI. Participants will explore why superficial knowledge is becoming less survivable, why AI still needs to be grounded in human reality, and how disciplined curiosity can help people remain valuable as AI becomes more capable. The session will include a short lecture-style presentation followed by a guided audience discussion. The discussion can be shaped around a small number of reflection questions, with flexibility to shift into Q&A or a brief example/demo depending on the audience engagement and MPL’s preference. No technical background is required. By the end of this session, participants will be able to: Explain why shallow learning and routine knowledge work become more vulnerable when AI can generate fluent answers quickly. Apply key machine learning principles, such as objective-setting, feedback, error correction, validation, calibration, and updating, as a practical framework for deeper human learning, better questioning, and stronger judgment. Bio: Darren Soo is a Canadian technology founder and creator of PI, an individualized AI reasoning framework designed to help people reason through complex, changing information over time. His background spans more than two decades of practical technology work across enterprise and operational software environments. His current work centres on artificial intelligence, machine learning, and explainable reasoning systems, while his broader interests include how technology can support curiosity, better questions, learning and decision-making.

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Aaniin
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Join an activity station! Activities include 'What's in the mystery box?', Kapla blocks, LEGO, colouring sheets, worksheets, and board games! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.

opportunities.title: AI Powered Job Search
opportunities.description: Are you using AI in your job search journey? Learn how to use AI to make your job search easier and more effective. In this workshop, you'll discover how AI can help you improve your resume, tailor it for Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), find jobs that match your skills, prepare for interviews, research employers, and stay organized throughout your job search. You'll also learn how to use AI safely and responsibly, with practical tips and prompts you can start using right away. No experience with AI is required. Learning outcomes: - discover how AI can help you improve your resume - discover how AI can help you with your whole job searching journey - learn how to use AI safely and responsibly in your job searching journey Presenter's bio: This workshop is facilitated by VPI Employment Services. Since 1988, VPI Employment Services have been delivering employment services to help individuals, employers, and communities achieve their goals at no cost . Their work focuses on providing tailored employment programs, vocational assessments, and supportive services to jobseekers that help build job readiness, provide access to training, and connect them with meaningful and sustainable employment opportunities.

opportunities.title: Creative Writing in the AI Apocalypse: Community Conversation with Joseph Donato
opportunities.description: How will writers survive the age of Artificial Intelligence?” Everyone’s got a story to tell, but the threat generative AI poses on the creative arts may discourage writers from putting pen to paper. Join this Community Conversation to understand the role of writers today, share your opinions on creative writing in an AI world, and engage with some related writing prompts. Joseph Donato is a Queer writer, editor, and library worker. He has completed his MFA in Creative Writing at the University of Guelph, and his most recent poetry chapbook, No One Should Be Happy When I'm Not was published in 2026. Joseph's poems have appeared in The Ampersand Review, Pinhole Magazine, and more. He enjoys dad rock, money, and being afraid. He can be found @josephdonato13 on Instagram or josephdonato.ca .

opportunities.title: Tips and Tricks to Master the IB Physics and IB Math Internal Assessment
opportunities.description: Join us for a 60-minute workshop designed to help IB students excel in their Internal Assessment (IA) for Math and Physics! Led by experienced IB educator and author of “7 Steps to a 7”, this session will provide valuable insights into the expectations and criteria for a successful IA. Learn how to choose a strong research question, avoid common pitfalls, manage your time effectively, and maximize your marks with expert tips and strategies. Whether you're just starting your IA or looking for guidance on revisions, this program will give you the tools you need to succeed in your IB coursework . Don’t miss out—sign up today! ** Please note: This program is run in partnership with Julia, a certified high school teacher of IB Physics SL and IB Math SL and creator of Physics in the Flesh (YouTube Channel) _____________________ Registrants will receive an email with the Zoom link 1 day prior to the program. If you do not receive the Zoom link the day before the program: Check your email inbox and spam folders. If you still cannot find the email, please contact us at mplcommunitylibrarians@markhamlibrary.ca prior to the program start time so we can provide you with the link.

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.description: 💻 Optimize Your Small Business with AI: Building Smart Workflows and AI Agents Artificial Intelligence is no longer just for large corporations. In this workshop, small business owners will learn how to leverage AI tools and AI agents to help streamline operations, such as tasks, ways to improve customer service, or increase productivity. Participants will explore how platforms such as Claude can be used to create customized AI workflows that support daily business activities. By the end of the program, attendees will have a clear understanding of how to identify opportunities for AI implementation and begin building AI-powered solutions tailored to their business needs. Learning Outcomes: Learn more about Claude and what it can do for small businesses Identify opportunities to use AI within their business Design and build simple AI agent workflows using Claude This workshop is presented in partnership with ENGR Solutions | Innovation in Artificial Intelligence

opportunities.title: Identifying AI Scams and Fakes
opportunities.description: Scams and fake media are getting more and more sophisticated with the use of artificial intelligence. This program teaches you how to spot AI-generated images, videos, and messages so you can protect yourself online. You'll learn strategies and tools to identify AI fraud scams, deepfakes, and disinformation on social media. A great session for digital literacy and online safety. Note: There will be a hands-on component to this program so we highly recommend bringing a laptop or mobile device so you can try out what we've talked about on your own!

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.description: Managing children's social media and AI usage often feels like a constant battle over restrictions. Parents frequently find themselves caught between enforcing rules and maintaining a positive, healthy relationship with their children. In this session, parents will: Understand the key online risks and platforms relevant to their children's age group Learn practical strategies and language to encourage healthy online habits and open dialogue at home Feel more confident supporting their children in becoming safe, responsible digital citizens Hosted by Kids Rights Canada .

opportunities.description: Beam yourself up to the Merril Collection of Science Fiction, Speculation and Fantasy and boldly embark on a 60-year journey that celebrates all things Star Trek! For decades, the original television series turned global franchise has inspired generations of fans, artists, and scientists alike. Visitors can explore voyages, characters, and new frontiers through our collection highlights such as novels, RPGs, fanzines, original artwork and more! This exhibit can be viewed during the Merril Collection's regular open hours.
